name: Question 21
problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{x+y}{x}
$$
worked_solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{x+y}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{x+(vx)}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{x(1+v)}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =1+v \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\ \int \,\text{d}v & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\ v & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}\,.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{x} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C \\ y & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+Cx.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the transformation y=v(x)x to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

dydx=x+yx

a
 y=xln⁡|x|+C
b
 y=2xln⁡|x|+Cx2
c
y=xln⁡|x|+Cx
d
 y=ln⁡|x|+Cx
e

Don't Know
Submit

EXPLANATION

With y=v(x)x, we have dydx=xdvdx+vddx(x)=xdvdx+v.

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

dydx=x+yxxdvdx+v=x+(vx)xxdvdx+v=x(1+v)xxdvdx+v=1+vxdvdx=1dvdx=1x.

Integrating both sides with respect to x, we obtain ∫dvdxdx=∫1xdx∫dv=∫1xdxv=ln⁡|x|+C.

From the transformation y=vx, we get v=yx. Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

yx=ln⁡|x|+Cy=xln⁡|x|+Cx.
